key: Nothing verifies that a harsh INSTRUCTIO
verdict: no behavioural form — the claim is about an absence of verification
why: The disclosure says nothing verifies that a harsh INSTRUCTION produced a harsh CRITIC. There is no run that could confirm it: a test would have to establish that no check anywhere measures critic harshness, which is a claim about the whole suite rather than about the loop's behaviour, and a passing test would only show that the one place it looked has no such check. Its truth rests on reading — the same footing the false decomposition claim rested on until it was caught, which is precisely why this is recorded rather than assumed. What WOULD settle it is a measurement of critic harshness, and there is none; that is the disclosure's point.

key: BOTH CRITICS SHARE A MODEL FAMILY
verdict: a fact about configuration, not about behaviour
why: Both critics are spawned as gauntlet-loop:gauntlet-ab-critic, so they share whatever model that agent definition resolves to. The stubbed harness answers every spawn itself and never resolves a model, so no run through it can observe a model family at all — a test would be asserting a property of the deployment rather than of the loop. What is checkable, and is checked elsewhere, is that both spawns name the same agentType; what is not checkable here is that the agentType maps to one family at run time.

verdict: no behavioural form — a claim about what does not exist
why: The disclosure says no calibration exists anywhere in the loop. A test cannot demonstrate the absence of a calibration step across a codebase; it can only fail to find one in the places it looks, which is weaker than the claim and would read as stronger. The honest support is the corpus and the run record: nothing in runs/ or oracle/ carries a calibration, and issue 29's rate and issue 25's builder measurement are the closest things to one, both of which postdate this sentence and neither of which calibrates the loop.

verdict: part of a longer blindness disclosure whose subject is the operator's filesystem
why: This phrase belongs to the disclosure about the candidate and reference standing in different relationships to the machine the run happens on — one is typically in the working tree and the other is not. The stubbed harness uses invented paths that exist nowhere, so no run through it can exhibit the asymmetry the sentence describes; observing it needs a real staging on a real disk. It is a property of how a run is set up, not of what the loop does with it.

key: FIND THOSE ORIGINALS AND DIFF BOTH
verdict: an instruction to the operator, not a claim about the loop
why: This clause tells the reader what to do — locate the originals of both artifacts and diff them — rather than asserting anything the loop does or does not do. There is no behaviour to drive: a test could confirm the sentence is present, which is exactly the presence-check this issue exists to distinguish from a truth-check. It is adjudicated rather than exercised because it has no truth condition of the kind the others have.

key: Critic and builder share a model family
verdict: a fact about configuration, not about behaviour
why: Same footing as BOTH CRITICS SHARE A MODEL FAMILY: the critic and builder are spawned as distinct agent types that resolve to models the harness never instantiates. A run through the stub cannot observe a family, so a test naming this disclosure would be asserting something it did not check — which is the failure this audit exists to make visible rather than to commit. The consequence the sentence draws, that the critic may be blind to exactly the mistakes the builder makes, is unmeasured and is a live gap rather than a covered one.

key: THE BLINDNESS PROBE MODELS THE FILESYSTE
verdict: partially checkable, and the part that matters is not
why: The disclosure says the probe models the filesystem only, while critic and builder both hold WebSearch and WebFetch — so a clean verdict means neither artifact gives away its origin TO A READER OF THIS DISK, and says nothing about the network. The first half is a property of the probe's prompt and could be read from source. The second half is the claim that matters and cannot be driven at all: demonstrating that a network channel is open requires a live agent with network access, which no test here may spawn. Recorded as unexercisable rather than half-tested, because a test covering only the checkable half would report this disclosure as verified while leaving its actual content untouched.

key: A NARROW WIN NO LONGER EXITS
why: The 3-2 judge split and the four `clear` margins come from a five-spawn run on one unchanged pair that predates the ledger discipline: it produced no machine-readable output, its figures live only in prose, and issue 50 examined that same run and REFUSED to reconstruct a ledger for it rather than manufacture one. So the number cannot be cited to a file that contains it. REPOINTED at decision 0007, which inverted what the sentence concludes: the disclosure used to say `margin` gates nothing BECAUSE the field reported high confidence on both sides of a split, and it now says the margin DOES gate and that this same unreliable field is what it gates on. The figure is unchanged and so is its problem — it still rests on a reading rather than a record, and it would still take a fresh q measurement to source it. What changed is that the figure is now cited as a COST being accepted rather than as a reason for inaction, which makes sourcing it more worth doing, not less.
